title: Memoisation and re-render rules
summary: When components re-render, memo and its shallow prop comparison, useMemo for expensive values, useCallback for stable functions, and when memoisation does not help.

sections.title: Why a component re-renders
sections.body:
A component re-renders when (1) its own state changes, (2) its parent re-renders, or (3) a context it reads changes. Changing props alone is not a trigger: props change because the parent re-rendered. Setting state to the **same value** (by `Object.is`) usually skips the render.

Re-rendering is normally cheap. Optimise only when you measure a slow interaction, for example with the React DevTools Profiler.

sections.title: memo
sections.body:
`const Row = memo(function Row(props) {…})` skips re-rendering `Row` when its parent re-renders with props that are **shallowly equal** to last time: each prop compared with `Object.is`. A new object, array or function created in the parent's render is a different reference every time, so it defeats `memo`.

`memo` does not stop re-renders caused by the component's own state or by a context it reads.

sections.title: useMemo and useCallback
sections.body:
`useMemo(() => compute(a, b), [a, b])` caches a **value** until a dependency changes. Use it for expensive calculations, or to keep an object or array reference stable for a memoised child or an effect dependency.

`useCallback(fn, deps)` caches a **function**; it is the same as `useMemo(() => fn, deps)`. It only helps when the function is passed to a `memo` component or used as a dependency. Wrapping every handler in `useCallback` adds cost and noise without benefit.

sections.title: Better than memoising
sections.body:
Before reaching for memoisation, try structural fixes:

- **Move state down** into the component that uses it, so fewer components re-render.
- **Lift content up** and pass it as `children`: children created by a parent do not re-render when a wrapper's state changes.
- Avoid unnecessary effects that set state.

The React Compiler can apply memoisation automatically at build time; when it is enabled, manual `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `memo` are rarely needed.

pitfalls: Passing inline objects or arrow functions to a `memo` child.
Expecting `memo` to block a context change or the component's own state change.
Missing dependencies in `useMemo` or `useCallback`, which return stale values.

gotchas.question: The parent re-renders. Does the memoised child re-render?
gotchas.code:
const Child = memo(({ style }: { style: object }) => <div style={style} />)
function Parent() { const [n, setN] = useState(0); return <Child style={{ color: "red" }} /> }
gotchas.answer: Yes. `{ color: "red" }` is a new object each render, so the shallow comparison fails.

gotchas.question: What is the difference between `useMemo(() => fn, [])` and `useCallback(fn, [])`?
gotchas.answer: None in result: both return the same `fn` reference across renders. `useCallback` is shorthand for memoising a function.

gotchas.question: A component calls `setCount(5)` when `count` is already 5. Does it re-render?
gotchas.answer: Usually not. React bails out when the new state is `Object.is`-equal to the current state (it may still call the component once before bailing out, but children and effects do not run).
